newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk coalition expects confidence vote on July 12.
newsitem.headline: Turk coalition expects confidence vote on July 12.

text.p: Turkey's new secularist coalition is expected to face a confidence vote in parliament on July 12 after the reading of the government programme on July 7, a government spokesman said on Monday.
"I expect there will be a confidence vote on July 12th," State Minister Ahad Andican told reporters after the first cabinet meeting of the government.
Andican said he expected parliament to begin debating the government programme on July 10, three days after it is read out in the assembly.
Secularist Mesut Yilmaz took over the post of prime minister from Islamist Necmettin Erbakan at a ceremony earlier on Monday.
President Suleyman Demirel appointed Yilmaz to replace Erbakan, who resigned two weeks ago amid disputes with the secularist army over Islamist activism.

Yilmaz's bid to win support for a government excluding the Islamists has been boosted by a wave of defections from a conservative faction allied with the Islamists. Yilmaz now has around 12 more MPs on paper than his opponents in the 550-member national assembly.
